statement: NVIDIA has cut Rubin Ultra's memory to 192GB HBM4 (8-Hi) from the previously expected 288GB (12-Hi), with tight HBM supply and data-center power limits cited as the drivers.
why: A flagship part shipping with a third to half less memory than planned is a direct read on how binding HBM allocation and rack power have become; it also cuts HBM content per accelerator across the coming generation.

impact.mechanism: Reducing stack height and capacity per GPU lowers each unit's claim on constrained HBM and rack power, letting more units ship, while cutting HBM bit demand per accelerator; the document states peak FLOPs are unchanged.

evidence.source: KuCoin News (citing SemiAnalysis via Huoxing Finance)
evidence.excerpt: The Rubin Ultra's core SKU will still use HBM4, with its theoretical peak FLOPs unchanged, but its HBM configuration has been reduced to 8-Hi and 192GB, down from the prior Rubin's 12-Hi and 288GB.

evidence.source: KuCoin News (citing SemiAnalysis via Huoxing Finance)
evidence.excerpt: tight HBM supply and data center power constraints

confidence.basis: Secondary aggregator relaying a research-house claim through a second outlet, with no NVIDIA confirmation in the document; the two accounts in the document disagree on the prior baseline.

dispersion: Prior baseline is reported as 288GB 12-Hi in the August 3 item but as 384GB HBM4E 12-Hi in the search-summarised September 1 follow-up; both describe the same despec to 192GB 8-Hi. The document flags this as an unreconciled discrepancy.
